﴿On the Day the sky will sway violently﴾: ﴿mawran﴾ means it will revolve like the turning of a millstone, and sway with its inhabitants like a ship tossing, and some of it will surge against other parts.

The expressions of the exegetes differed concerning it. Ibn 'Abbas said: it will revolve in a revolving motion. Qatadah: it will move. al-Dahhak: it will shake. 'Ata' al-Khurasani: some of its parts will differ from one another. Qutrub: it will be agitated. 'Atiyyah: it will differ. al-Mu'arrikh: some of its parts will shift, shifting. al-Akhfash: it will sway, and all these meanings are close to one another.

The root of ﴿al-mawr﴾ is difference and agitation. Ru'bah said:

"Blackened at the upper arms, marked by the vein's tracery,
Swaying at the shoulder-blades, its neck held upright."

That is, its two arms are agitated.

﴿And the mountains will be set in motion, moving﴾: they will depart from their places and become scattered dust.

﴿Woe that Day to the deniers﴾. The reason the particle ﴿fa'﴾ was placed before ﴿woe﴾ is that the speech contains the sense of ﴿mujazah﴾ (a conditional, implied-consequence construction). Its meaning is: if this is so, then ﴿woe that Day to the deniers﴾.

﴿Who are in [vain] discourse, playing﴾: heedless, ignorant, forgetful and careless.

﴿The Day they will be pushed toward the fire of Hell with a [violent] pushing﴾: they will be thrust toward it and driven toward it with force. That is because the keepers of the Fire will chain their hands to their necks, gather their forelocks to their feet, and then push them into the Fire, face-first, while their napes are thrust back, until they reach the Fire.

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi recited ﴿yawma yud'awna ilā al-nār du'ā'an﴾ with the lighter form, from ﴿du'ā'﴾ (calling). They said: when they draw near the Fire, the keepers will say to them:

﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny. Is this magic, or is it that you do not see? Burn therein; so be patient or be not patient; it is all the same for you. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do. Indeed, the righteous will be within gardens and pleasure, enjoying what their Lord has given them, and their Lord has protected them from the punishment of Hellfire.﴾ ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you used to do, reclining on thrones arranged in rows﴾, meaning some placed beside others and facing one another. ﴿And We will marry them to fair-eyed maidens﴾.

﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith﴾: Abu 'Amr recited ﴿wa-atba'nāhum﴾ with nūn and alif, and ﴿dhurriyyātuhum﴾ with alif in both places, with the taa' in both vowelled with kasrah, in accordance with the words ﴿alḥaqnā﴾ ... ﴿wa mā ālatnāhum﴾, so that the speech would be of one pattern. The others recited ﴿wa-ittaba'tahum﴾ with taa' and without alif. Then they differed concerning ﴿dhurriyyatuhum﴾: the people of Madinah recited the first without alif and with a ḍammah on the taa', and the second with alif and a kasrah on the taa'; the people of Syria recited both with alif and a kasrah on the taa' of the second; this is the choice of Ya'qub and Abu Hatim; and the others recited both without alif, with a fatḥah on the taa' of the second; this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd.

**Al-Tha'alibi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 52, verses 25–49:**

﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning each other.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: this is when they are raised from their graves. Others said: it is in Paradise, and this is the more correct view, because of His saying: ﴿We were before this, among our people, fearful [of God's punishment]. But God has been gracious to us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind.﴾ Al-Hasan said: al-Samum (the scorching wind) is one of the names of Hell.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: my father related to us, saying: Anas ibn 'Iyad related to us, saying: Shayba ibn Nisah related to me, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: I went out one day, and whenever I went out I would begin by greeting 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. I found her one day praying al-Subha [al-Subha: voluntary and supererogatory prayer], reciting ﴿But God has been gracious to us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾ and repeating it, weeping. I stood there until I grew weary, then I went to the market for my business, and then I returned, and she was still reciting it, repeating it, weeping and supplicating.

﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him﴾ in the world, devoting worship to Him. The word ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ (innahu, "indeed He") was read by al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and al-Kisa'i with a fathah on the alif (أَنَّهُ), meaning "because He," and this is the choice of Abu Hatim. The others read it with a kasrah (إِنَّهُ), as a new sentence, and this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayda. ﴿He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: al-Latif (the Subtle, Gracious). Al-Dahhak said: al-Sadiq (the Truthful) in what He promised.

﴿So remind, [O Muhammad]. You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a soothsayer or a madman.﴾ "By the favour of your Lord" means by His mercy and protection. A soothsayer (kahin) is one who invents speech and reports what will happen tomorrow without revelation. A kahin is also one who claims that he has a companion from the jinn.

This verse was revealed concerning the slanderers (al-kharrasun) who divided among themselves the paths of Makkah, turning people away from faith, and who accused the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of soothsaying, madness, sorcery and poetry. This is His saying:

﴿Or do they say, "[He is] a poet; we await for him the misfortunes of time"?﴾ That is, these dividers and slanderers say: we await for him the calamities of time, so that it will suffice us to deal with him, by death or a destructive event, and he will die and his companions will scatter. They said: we await for him the angel of death, so that he will perish as those poets before him perished, such as Zuhayr, al-Nabigha and so-and-so and so-and-so. They said: he is only like one of them, and his father died young, and we hope that his death will be like his father's death.

Al-Manun may mean "time" (al-dahr) and may mean "death." They were named so because they diminish and cut off the term of life. Al-Akhfash said: because they weaken the strength of a person and his vigour (manih), that is, they diminish them. Ibn 'Abbas recited:

*Wait for her, the calamity of time, perhaps she will
divorce one day, or her husband will die.*

[[Lisan al-'Arab: 7/40.]]

﴿Say: "Wait, and I am with you among those who wait."﴾ Until the command of Allah comes upon you.

﴿Or do their minds command them to this?﴾ That is, their intellects. In the pre-Islamic period they used to call the people of intellect (ahlam) and describe them as wise. It was said to 'Amr ibn al-'As: what is the matter with your people that they do not believe, when Allah has described them as possessing intellect? He said: those are intellects that Allah has outwitted, meaning that success (tawfiq) did not accompany them. ﴿Or are they a transgressing people?﴾ Rather, they are a transgressing people.

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ Rather, they do not believe, out of arrogance.

﴿Then let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful﴾ that Muhammad invented it from his own self. For the tongue is their tongue, and they are equal to him in humanity, language and strength. ﴿like it﴾ means like this Qur'an, resembling it.

﴿Or were they created from nothing?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: without a Lord. It was also said: without a father or mother, so they are like inanimate things that do not understand, and Allah has no argument against them. Did they not get created from a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh? This was said by Ibn 'Ata'. Ibn Kaysan said: or were they created in vain, left neglected, neither commanded nor forbidden? This is like the saying of someone: "I did such-and-such for no reason," meaning for no purpose. ﴿Or are they the creators [of themselves]?﴾

﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they have no certainty.﴾ ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: the rain and provision. 'Ikrima said: it means prophethood. It was also said: knowledge of what will occur. ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ That is, the dominant, the tyrants. This was said by most of the exegetes, and it is the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ata' said: lords who dominate. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is said, "Khawwala tasaytara 'alayya," meaning: he took me as a subordinate. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿or are they the ones who bring down [revelation]?﴾

﴿Or do they have a ladder﴾ [claiming that they have] a means of ascent and a stairway by which they climb to the heavens, ﴿upon which they listen﴾ to the revelation, so they claim that they heard there that what they are upon is the truth, and so they hold fast to it for that reason. ﴿Then let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ [a proof] if they claim that.

﴿Or do you ask them for payment, so they are burdened with debt?﴾ That is, a reward for what you brought them and what you called them to. ﴿burdened﴾ means overburdened.

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so they record it?﴾ That is, knowledge of what is hidden from them, so that they know that what the Messenger tells them about the Resurrection, the raising, the reckoning, reward and punishment is false and will not come to pass. Qatada said: when they said ﴿We await for him the misfortunes of time﴾, Allah revealed ﴿Or do they have the unseen?﴾, so that they know even the death of Muhammad and what his affair will come to. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, do they have the Preserved Tablet, so that they write what is in it and inform the people of it? Al-Qutabi said: ﴿so they record﴾ means they judge.

Al-Kitab means judgment, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the two men who disputed: «I will judge between you by the Book of Allah» [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/478.]]

meaning by the judgment of Allah.

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ Deception in the Dar al-Nadwa (the Meeting House of Quraysh). ﴿But those who disbelieve, it is they who will be plotted against.﴾ The harm of the plot returns upon them, and the deception encompasses them. All of that happened when they were killed at Badr.

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: everything in Surat al-Tur mentioning ﴿أَمْ﴾ (am, "or") is interrogative and not conjunctive.

﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling down﴾ kisfan (a piece) is a fragment, and it was said: pieces, its singular being kisfa, like sidra and sidr (lote tree and lote trees). ﴿falling down﴾ the word is mentioned in the form of kisf. ﴿they would say﴾ out of their obstinacy, excessive stupidity and wretched persistence, ﴿"This is a layered cloud"﴾ placed one upon another.

This is a reply to their saying: ﴿Cause fragments of the sky to fall upon us﴾ and their saying: ﴿Or make the sky fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed﴾. He said: if we did this, they would say, "a layered cloud."

﴿So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck unconscious﴾ that is, they will die. Al-A'mash, 'Asim and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿يُصْعَقُونَ﴾ (yus'aqun) with a dammah on the yaʾ and a fathah on the ʿayn, meaning they will be destroyed. Al-Farra' said: both are dialects, like sa'd and su'd.

﴿The Day when their plot will avail them nothing, nor will they be helped. And indeed, for those who have wronged﴾ that is, disbelieved, ﴿is a punishment short of that.﴾ Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: it is the punishment of the grave. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is killing at Badr. Mujahid said: hunger and famine for seven years. Ibn Zayd said: the calamities that strike them, the pains, and the loss of wealth and children. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ that the punishment is descending upon them.

﴿And be patient for the decree of your Lord, for indeed you are in Our eyes﴾ in Our sight and view. ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ Abu al-Ahwas 'Awf ibn Malik, 'Ata' and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: say, "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You) when you rise from your gathering. If the gathering was good, you will gain more reward, and if it was otherwise, it will be an expiation for it.

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Saqlab related to us, saying: Ibn al-Hasan Ahmad ibn 'Isa ibn Hamdun al-Naqid in Tartus related to us, saying: Abu Umayya related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj related to us, saying: Musa ibn 'Uqba informed me, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayra, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: «Whoever sits in a gathering in which there is much noise, and before he rises says: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; there is no god but You; I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance), he will be forgiven for whatever occurred in that gathering» [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/494.]].

Ibn Zayd said: [glorify] by the command of your Lord ﴿when you arise﴾ from your sleep. Al-Dahhak and al-Rabi' said: when you rise to prayer, say: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabaraka ismuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god other than You). Also from al-Dahhak: that is, say when you rise to prayer: "Allahu akbar kabiran, wal-hamdu lillahi kathiran, wa subhan Allahi bukratan wa asila" (Allah is greatest, greatly; praise be to Allah, abundantly; and glory be to Allah, morning and evening). Al-Kalbi said: it means the remembrance of Allah with the tongue when you rise from your bed until you enter prayer. It was also said: it is the Fajr prayer.

﴿And during the night glorify Him﴾ that is, pray to Him, meaning the two prayers of 'Isha'. ﴿And at the retreat of the stars.﴾

'Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and Anas ibn Malik said: it means the two rak'as of Fajr.

'Aqil informed me, saying: al-Maqabi related to us, saying: Ibn Jarir related to us, saying: Bisr related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Qatada related to us, on the authority of Zurara ibn Awfa, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Hisham, on the authority of 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the two rak'as of Fajr: «They are better than the whole world» [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/149.]].

Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: it is the obligatory Subh prayer.

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd read ﴿وَأَدْبارِ﴾ (wa-adbar, "and the backs") with a fathah on the alif (وَأَدْبارَ, "and the endings"), and similarly Zayd narrated from Ya'qub. That is: after the setting of the stars.

Mujahid said: hunger and famine for seven years. Ibn Zayd said: the calamities that strike them, the pains, and the loss of wealth and children. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ that the punishment is descending upon them.

﴿And be patient for the decree of your Lord, for indeed you are in Our eyes﴾ in Our sight and view. ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ Abu al-Ahwas 'Awf ibn Malik, 'Ata' and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: say, "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You) when you rise from your gathering. If the gathering was good, you will gain more reward, and if it was otherwise, it will be an expiation for it.

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Saqlab related to us, saying: Ibn al-Hasan Ahmad ibn 'Isa ibn Hamdun al-Naqid in Tartus related to us, saying: Abu Umayya related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj related to us, saying: Musa ibn 'Uqba informed me, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayra, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: «Whoever sits in a gathering in which there is much noise, and before he rises says: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; there is no god but You; I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance), he will be forgiven for whatever occurred in that gathering» [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/494.]].

Ibn Zayd said: [glorify] by the command of your Lord ﴿when you arise﴾ from your sleep. Al-Dahhak and al-Rabi' said: when you rise to prayer, say: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabaraka ismuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god other than You). Al-Kalbi said: it means the remembrance of Allah with the tongue when you rise from your bed until you enter prayer. It was also said: it is the Fajr prayer.

﴿And during the night glorify Him﴾ that is, pray to Him, meaning the two prayers of 'Isha'. ﴿And at the retreat of the stars.﴾

'Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and Anas ibn Malik said: it means the two rak'as of Fajr.

'Aqil informed me, saying: al-Maqabi related to us, saying: Ibn Jarir related to us, saying: Bisr related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Qatada related to us, on the authority of Zurara ibn Awfa, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Hisham, on the authority of 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the two rak'as of Fajr: «They are better than the whole world» [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/149.]].

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd read ﴿وَأَدْبارِ﴾ (wa-adbar, "and the backs") with a fathah on the alif (وَأَدْبارَ, "and the endings"), and similarly Zayd narrated from Ya'qub. That is: after the setting of the stars.

**Al-Tha'alibi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 52, verses 25–49:**

﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning each other.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: this is when they are raised from their graves. Others said: it is in Paradise, and this is the more correct view, because of His saying: ﴿We were before this, among our people, fearful [of God's punishment]. But God has been gracious to us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind.﴾ Al-Hasan said: al-Samum (the scorching wind) is one of the names of Hell.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: my father related to us, saying: Anas ibn 'Iyad related to us, saying: Shayba ibn Nisah related to me, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: I went out one day, and whenever I went out I would begin by greeting 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. I found her one day praying al-Subha [al-Subha: voluntary and supererogatory prayer], reciting ﴿But God has been gracious to us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾ and repeating it, weeping. I stood there until I grew weary, then I went to the market for my business, and then I returned, and she was still reciting it, repeating it, weeping and supplicating.

﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him﴾ in the world, devoting worship to Him. The word ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ (innahu, "indeed He") was read by al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and al-Kisa'i with a fathah on the alif (أَنَّهُ), meaning "because He," and this is the choice of Abu Hatim. The others read it with a kasrah (إِنَّهُ), as a new sentence, and this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayda. ﴿He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: al-Latif (the Subtle, Gracious). Al-Dahhak said: al-Sadiq (the Truthful) in what He promised.

﴿So remind, [O Muhammad]. You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a soothsayer or a madman.﴾ "By the favour of your Lord" means by His mercy and protection. A soothsayer (kahin) is one who invents speech and reports what will happen tomorrow without revelation. A kahin is also one who claims that he has a companion from the jinn.

This verse was revealed concerning the slanderers (al-kharrasun) who divided among themselves the paths of Makkah, turning people away from faith, and who accused the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of soothsaying, madness, sorcery and poetry. This is His saying:

﴿Or do they say, "[He is] a poet; we await for him the misfortunes of time"?﴾ That is, these dividers and slanderers say: we await for him the calamities of time, so that it will suffice us to deal with him, by death or a destructive event, and he will die and his companions will scatter. They said: we await for him the angel of death, so that he will perish as those poets before him perished, such as Zuhayr, al-Nabigha and so-and-so and so-and-so. They said: he is only like one of them, and his father died young, and we hope that his death will be like his father's death.

Al-Manun may mean "time" (al-dahr) and may mean "death." They were named so because they diminish and cut off the term of life. Al-Akhfash said: because they weaken the strength of a person and his vigour (manih), that is, they diminish them. Ibn 'Abbas recited:

*Wait for her, the calamity of time, perhaps she will
divorce one day, or her husband will die.*

[[Lisan al-'Arab: 7/40.]]

﴿Say: "Wait, and I am with you among those who wait."﴾ Until the command of Allah comes upon you.

﴿Or do their minds command them to this?﴾ That is, their intellects. In the pre-Islamic period they used to call the people of intellect (ahlam) and describe them as wise. It was said to 'Amr ibn al-'As: what is the matter with your people that they do not believe, when Allah has described them as possessing intellect? He said: those are intellects that Allah has outwitted, meaning that success (tawfiq) did not accompany them. ﴿Or are they a transgressing people?﴾ Rather, they are a transgressing people.

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ Rather, they do not believe, out of arrogance.

﴿Then let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful﴾ that Muhammad invented it from his own self. For the tongue is their tongue, and they are equal to him in humanity, language and strength. ﴿like it﴾ means like this Qur'an, resembling it.

﴿Or were they created from nothing?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: without a Lord. It was also said: without a father or mother, so they are like inanimate things that do not understand, and Allah has no argument against them. Did they not get created from a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh? This was said by Ibn 'Ata'. Ibn Kaysan said: or were they created in vain, left neglected, neither commanded nor forbidden? This is like the saying of someone: "I did such-and-such for no reason," meaning for no purpose. ﴿Or are they the creators [of themselves]?﴾

﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they have no certainty.﴾ ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: the rain and provision. 'Ikrima said: it means prophethood. It was also said: knowledge of what will occur. ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ That is, the dominant, the tyrants. This was said by most of the exegetes, and it is the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ata' said: lords who dominate. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is said, "Khawwala tasaytara 'alayya," meaning: he took me as a subordinate. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿or are they the ones who bring down [revelation]?﴾

﴿Or do they have a ladder﴾ [claiming that they have] a means of ascent and a stairway by which they climb to the heavens, ﴿upon which they listen﴾ to the revelation, so they claim that they heard there that what they are upon is the truth, and so they hold fast to it for that reason. ﴿Then let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ [a proof] if they claim that.

﴿Or do you ask them for payment, so they are burdened with debt?﴾ That is, a reward for what you brought them and what you called them to. ﴿burdened﴾ means overburdened.

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so they record it?﴾ That is, knowledge of what is hidden from them, so that they know that what the Messenger tells them about the Resurrection, the raising, the reckoning, reward and punishment is false and will not come to pass. Qatada said: when they said ﴿We await for him the misfortunes of time﴾, Allah revealed ﴿Or do they have the unseen?﴾, so that they know even the death of Muhammad and what his affair will come to. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, do they have the Preserved Tablet, so that they write what is in it and inform the people of it? Al-Qutabi said: ﴿so they record﴾ means they judge.

Al-Kitab means judgment, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the two men who disputed: «I will judge between you by the Book of Allah» [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/478.]]

meaning by the judgment of Allah.

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ Deception in the Dar al-Nadwa (the Meeting House of Quraysh). ﴿But those who disbelieve, it is they who will be plotted against.﴾ The harm of the plot returns upon them, and the deception encompasses them. All of that happened when they were killed at Badr.

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: everything in Surat al-Tur mentioning ﴿أَمْ﴾ (am, "or") is interrogative and not conjunctive.

﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling down﴾ kisfan (a piece) is a fragment, and it was said: pieces, its singular being kisfa, like sidra and sidr (lote tree and lote trees). ﴿falling down﴾ the word is mentioned in the form of kisf. ﴿they would say﴾ out of their obstinacy, excessive stupidity and wretched persistence, ﴿"This is a layered cloud"﴾ placed one upon another.

This is a reply to their saying: ﴿Cause fragments of the sky to fall upon us﴾ and their saying: ﴿Or make the sky fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed﴾. He said: if we did this, they would say, "a layered cloud."

﴿So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck unconscious﴾ that is, they will die. Al-A'mash, 'Asim and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿يُصْعَقُونَ﴾ (yus'aqun) with a dammah on the yaʾ and a fathah on the ʿayn, meaning they will be destroyed. Al-Farra' said: both are dialects, like sa'd and su'd.
